summary: Quantizes selected attribute values into discrete levels using floor, round, ceiling, comparison-to-zero logic, value steps, offsets, and optional type casting. It is the focused attribute-quantization counterpart to the quantize controls found in broader math operators.

key_params.name: group
key_params.note: Optional group limiting which elements are affected

key_params.name: inputattrscope
key_params.note: Input attribute or components to quantize

key_params.name: parsize
key_params.note: Number of independently controlled component lanes

key_params.name: quantize
key_params.note: Off, floor, round, ceiling, or logical comparison modes

key_params.name: quantoffset
key_params.note: Offset applied to the quantization grid

key_params.name: quantcompare
key_params.note: Comparison value for logical quantize modes

key_params.name: castto
key_params.note: Automatic, float, or int output casting

key_params.name: attrtype
key_params.note: Manual output attribute type when overriding automatic output

key_params.name: attrdefaultval
key_params.note: Default output value if quantization cannot be computed

key_concepts: Quantize POP converts continuous or arbitrary selected attribute values into discrete steps or comparison results.
Parameter Size, step, offset, and compare controls define independent component quantization lanes.
Output casting and output-attribute override controls let quantized data become integer masks, float attributes, or custom typed outputs.
common_gotchas: Use Parameter Size to match the selected components; otherwise all components may share the same quantize settings.
Logical modes such as greater-than-zero produce binary-style attributes, which can be useful as masks but destructive for continuous data.
Quantize can introduce discontinuities; use it late in a signal chain or keep the original continuous attribute under a separate name.
